newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil NNE sugar exports running well ex-Recife.
newsitem.headline: Brazil NNE sugar exports running well ex-Recife.

text.p: Exports of the 1996/97 sugar crop from the Brazil's north/northeast crop out of the port of Recife are already higher than last year for the month of September, according to port's docking manager.
So far this month, two ships have loaded a total of 18,069 tonnes of bulk sugar while last week, the Emel II left carrying 5,500 tonnes of bagged sugar, Alexandre Nobrega said.
The Aposteles II is currently loading 12,545 tonnes of sugar in bags after arriving on September 18, Nobrega said. The ship is expected to leave the port by October 8.
There are no other sugar ships scheduled to arrive at present, he added.
Last year, Recife saw exports of 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar only during the entire month of September.
The port has 16 berths available for sugar loading, one of which is a bulk terminal which has a nominal capacity of 1,000 tonnes an hour, Nobrega said.
In Maceio, the port has yet to see any exports of 1996/97 north/northeast sugar, a port official said.
The port, which has three berths, currently has 967 tonnes of old crop sugar and 8,890 tonnes of current crop sugar in its warehouses.
The next sugar vessel is due to arrive on October 2 to load 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar, the official said.
Maceio and Recife are the two key ports for the north/northeast producing region where the harvest runs from September to the end of April.
Exports from the region are expected by the government to reach around 1.52 million tonnes although independent analysts think the figure could end up nearer to 1.75 million tonnes.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
